fact: Microbial molecules that stimulate innate immunity and are shared by classes of microbes are called pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs).
quote: The microbial substances that stimulate innate immunity are often shared by classes of microbes and are called pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs).

fact: Typical PAMPs are double-stranded RNA of replicating viruses, unmethylated CpG DNA of bacteria, N-formylmethionine-initiated proteins, LPS, lipoteichoic acid and terminal-mannose oligosaccharides.
quote: long double-stranded RNA found in replicating viruses and unmethylated CpG DNA sequences found in bacteria

fact: Damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are endogenous molecules that damaged or dying cells release; they can signal sterile injury such as burns, trauma or ischaemia.
quote: These substances are called damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs)

fact: Examples of DAMPs are heat shock proteins, monosodium urate crystals, extracellular formylated peptides and ATP, extracellular HMGB1, histones and cytoplasmic dsDNA.
quote: Extracellular HMGB1, histones, cytoplasmic dsDNA

fact: Cellular pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) are located on the cell surface, in phagocytic vesicles (endosomes) and in the cytosol; soluble recognition molecules are in blood and secretions.
quote: These receptors are located on the surfaces, in phagocytic vesicles, and in the cytosol of various cell types

fact: Humans have 10 functional TLRs, TLR1 to TLR10.
quote: There are 10 different functional TLRs in humans, named TLR1 through TLR10

fact: The function of TLR10 is poorly understood; it may have anti-inflammatory functions, unlike all other TLRs.
quote: there is some evidence that it may have anti-inflammatory functions, unlike all the other TLRs

fact: The Toll/IL-1 receptor (TIR) domain in the TLR cytoplasmic tail is also present in the receptors for IL-1, IL-18 and IL-33.
quote: TIR domains are also found in the cytoplasmic tails of the receptors for the cytokines IL-1, IL-18, and IL-33

fact: TLR1, TLR2, TLR4, TLR5 and TLR6 are on the plasma membrane and recognize extracellular bacterial and fungal PAMPs.
quote: TLRs 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 are expressed on the plasma membrane

fact: TLR3, TLR7, TLR8 and TLR9 are mainly on endosomal membranes and detect microbial nucleic acids.
quote: TLRs 3, 7, 8, and 9 are mainly expressed inside cells on endosomal membranes

fact: Endosomal TLRs distinguish microbial from host nucleic acids by location, because host RNA is not normally present in endosomes.
quote: the endosomal TLRs may distinguish nucleic acids of normal cells from microbial nucleic acids on the basis of the cellular location

fact: LPS of gram-negative bacteria binds TLR4; peptidoglycan and lipoteichoic acid of gram-positive bacteria bind TLR2.
quote: LPS of gram-negative bacteria, which binds TLR4; and peptidoglycan and lipoteichoic acid of gram-positive bacteria, which bind TLR2.

fact: Flagellin of motile bacteria binds TLR5.
quote: flagellin, a protein subunit component of the flagella of motile bacteria, which binds to TLR5.

fact: Double-stranded RNA binds TLR3; viral single-stranded RNA in endosomes binds TLR7 and TLR8.
quote: double-stranded RNAs, which are present in viruses but not mammalian cells, bind to TLR3

fact: Unmethylated CpG motifs, common in prokaryotic DNA but rare in vertebrate genomes, bind TLR9.
quote: unmethylated CpG nucleotide repeats, which are common in prokaryotic DNA but rare in vertebrate genomes, bind to TLR9.

fact: In mammalian genomic DNA, CpG dinucleotides are heavily methylated; in bacteria and many viruses they stay unmethylated and act as a PAMP.
quote: In mammalian genomes, CpG dinucleotides in genomic DNA are heavily methylated on the cytosine by DNA methyltransferases.

fact: TLR9 recognizes unmethylated CpG DNA of bacteria and herpesviruses and is expressed by plasmacytoid dendritic cells, B cells, eosinophils and basophils.
quote: TLR-9 DNA with unmethylated CpG (bacteria and herpesviruses) Plasmacytoid dendritic cells, eosinophils, B cells, basophils

fact: TLR9-deficient plasmacytoid dendritic cells cannot make type I interferons in response to herpes simplex virus.
quote: the inability of TLR-9-deficient plasmacytoid dendritic cells to generate type I interferons in response to herpes simplex virus

fact: The TLR1:TLR2 heterodimer recognizes triacyl lipopeptides and the TLR2:TLR6 heterodimer recognizes diacyl lipopeptides.
quote: The diacyl and triacyl lipopeptides recognized by the heterodimeric receptors TLR-6:TLR-2 and TLR-1:TLR-2, respectively

fact: LPS first binds soluble LPS-binding protein; the accessory protein MD2 binds lipid A of LPS and the complex then engages TLR4.
quote: An extracellular protein called MD2 (myeloid differentiation protein 2) binds to the lipid A component of LPS

fact: CD14 is also required for efficient LPS-induced TLR4 signalling.
quote: Another protein, called CD14, is also required for efficient LPS-induced signaling.

fact: The protein UNC93B moves TLRs from the endoplasmic reticulum to endosomes; deficiency of TLR3 or UNC93B causes susceptibility to herpes simplex virus encephalitis.
quote: Genetic deficiency in TLR3 or UNC93B leads to susceptibility to certain viral infections, especially herpes simplex virus encephalitis

fact: NF-κB induces inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-1), chemokines (CCL2, CXCL8) and endothelial adhesion molecules (E-selectin).
quote: inflammatory cytokines (e.g., tumor necrosis factor [TNF] and IL-1), chemokines (e.g., CCL2 and CXCL8), and endothelial adhesion molecules (e.g., E-selectin)

fact: IRF3 and IRF7, together with NF-κB, induce the type I interferons IFN-α and IFN-β.
quote: IRF3 and IRF7, together with NF-κB, promote the expression of genes encoding interferon (IFN)-α and IFN-β

fact: All TLRs except TLR3 use the adaptor MyD88; only TLR3 and TLR4 use the adaptor TRIF.
quote: All TLRs except TLR3 engage the adaptor MyD88, while only TLR3 and TLR4 utilize the adaptor TRIF

fact: Mammalian TLRs use four TIR-containing adaptors: MyD88, MAL, TRIF and TRAM.
quote: There are four such adaptors used by mammalian TLRs: MyD88 (myeloid differentiation factor 88), MAL

fact: TLR5, TLR7 and TLR9 use only MyD88; TLR3 uses only TRIF; TLR2 heterodimers use MyD88/MAL; TLR4 uses MyD88/MAL and TRIF/TRAM.
quote: TLR-4 signaling uses both of these adaptor pairs, MyD88/MAL and TRIF/TRAM.

fact: MyD88 binds the TLR through its TIR domain; the MyD88 death domain recruits and activates the kinases IRAK4 and IRAK1.
quote: the death domain recruits and activates two serine-threonine protein kinases—IRAK4 (IL1-receptor associated kinase 4) and IRAK1

fact: IRAK recruits TRAF6, which leads to activation of TAK1 and the IKK complex (IKKα, IKKβ, IKKγ/NEMO); IKK phosphorylates IκB, which releases NF-κB to induce TNF, IL-1β and IL-6.
quote: Activated IKK phosphory-lates IkB, which then releases NF«B.

fact: The endosomal TLR7, TLR8 and TLR9 also use MyD88, but this signalling activates IRFs and induces type I IFN antiviral responses.
quote: The endosomal TLRs 7, 8, and 9 also engage MyD88

fact: MyD88 binds IRF7 directly in endosomes, so TLR7 and TLR9 induce IFN-α and IFN-β in plasmacytoid dendritic cells.
quote: the endosomal TLRs—TLR-7 and TLR-9—can activate IRF7, resulting in the production of IFN-a and IFN-f by cells such as plasmacytoid dendritic cells

fact: Cell-surface TLR4 uses both MyD88 and TRIF and activates NF-κB, IRF3 and IRF7, giving inflammatory and antiviral responses.
quote: Cell surface TLR4 engages both MyD88 and TRIF, leading to NF-κB, IRF3 and IRF7 activation

fact: Endosomal TLR3 signals only through TRIF, which activates NF-κB and IRF3.
quote: Endosomal TLR3 signals only through TRIF, which activates NF-κB and IRF3.

fact: TRIF activates the kinases IKKε and TBK1, which phosphorylate IRF3 and induce IFN-β.
quote: binds and activates the kinases IkKe and TBK1. These in turn phosphorylate IRF3, which induces the expression of IFN-B.

fact: TLR activation induces the co-stimulatory molecules CD80 (B7.1) and CD86 (B7.2) on dendritic cells and macrophages, which are essential to start adaptive immunity.
quote: called B7.1 (CD80) and B7.2 (CD86), are expressed by both macrophages and tissue dendritic cells in response to activation by pathogen sensors such as TLRs

fact: Patients with MyD88 or IRAK4 mutations have severe invasive bacterial infections early in life, especially pneumococcal pneumonia; infections become less severe later.
quote: Individuals with mutations in MyD88 and IRAK4 have severe, invasive bacterial infections early in life, especially pneumococcal pneumonia.

fact: Patients with MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency usually cannot mount a fever during illness.
quote: these patients are usually unable to mount a fever in the setting of illness.

fact: Autosomal recessive MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency causes recurrent invasive pyogenic infections with little inflammation ('cold' infections).
quote: recurrent, severe peripheral, and invasive infections by pyogenic bacteria that elicit little inflammation, a situation known as a ‘cold’ infection

fact: In human IRAK4 deficiency, no extra susceptibility to viral infections is seen.
quote: In human IRAK4 deficiency, for example, no extra susceptibility to viral infections has been noted.

fact: Loss-of-function TLR3 mutations cause recurrent herpes simplex encephalitis without a general increase in other viral infections.
quote: TLR3 loss of function mutations can result in recurrent herpes simplex encephalitis.

fact: Autosomal recessive TRIF mutations and autosomal dominant TRAF3 or TBK1 mutations also cause susceptibility to herpes simplex encephalitis.
quote: Autosomal recessive mutations in TRIF and autosomal dominant mutations affecting the TRAF3 E3 ligase also result in susceptibility to herpes simplex encephalitis.

fact: Homozygous UNC93B mutations reduce type I IFN production and increase susceptibility to herpes simplex encephalitis.
quote: Homozygous mutations in UNC93B result in reduced type 1 IFN generation and increased susceptibility to herpes simplex encephalitis.

fact: NEMO deficiency blocks NF-κB activation downstream of all TLRs and so affects both innate and adaptive immunity.
quote: also impairs TLR signaling though its block of normal NF«B activation downstream of all TLRs

fact: X-linked EDA-ID (anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with immunodeficiency), usually from NEMO or IKKβ mutations, impairs TLR and CD40 signalling and causes infections with pyogenic bacteria, mycobacteria, viruses and Pneumocystis.
quote: These patients suffer from infections with encapsulated pyogenic bacteria as well as with intracellular bacterial pathogens, including mycobacteria, viruses, and fungi such as P. jirovecii.

fact: NOD1 recognizes diaminopimelic acid (DAP), mainly from gram-negative peptidoglycan.
quote: NOD1 recognizes a glycosylated tripeptide called diaminopimelic acid (DAP), derived mainly from gram-negative bacterial peptidoglycan

fact: NOD2 recognizes muramyl dipeptide (MDP) from peptidoglycan of gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria.
quote: NOD2 recognizes a distinct molecule called muramyl dipeptide (MDP), derived from peptidoglycans of both gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria.

fact: Activated NOD1/NOD2 recruit the kinase RIP2, which activates NF-κB.
quote: the CARD effector domains of the NOD proteins to recruit many molecules of the kinase RIP2

fact: Some NOD2 polymorphisms increase the risk of Crohn's disease, probably through defective sensing of intestinal microbes.
quote: Certain NOD2 gene polymorphisms increase the risk for an inflammatory disease of the bowel called Crohn’s disease.

fact: Gain-of-function NOD2 mutations cause the systemic inflammatory disease Blau syndrome.
quote: gain-of-function mutations of NOD2 that cause increased NOD signaling and NF-κB activation lead to a systemic inflammatory disease called Blau syndrome

fact: Blau syndrome causes spontaneous inflammation in the joints, eyes and skin.
quote: Blau syndrome, which is characterized by spontaneous inflammation in the joints, eyes, and skin.

fact: Inflammasomes are cytosolic multiprotein complexes that form in response to infection or cell injury and generate active caspase-1.
quote: Inflammasomes are multiprotein enzymatic complexes that form in the cytosol in response to infections or cell injury

fact: Oligomerized NLRP3 binds the adaptor ASC; ASC filaments recruit procaspase-1, which clusters and becomes active caspase-1.
quote: each NLRP3 protein in the oligomer binds an adaptor protein called ASC (apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD).

fact: The main function of caspase-1 is to cleave the inactive precursors of IL-1β and IL-18 into active cytokines.
quote: the main function of caspase-1 is to cleave the inactive cytoplasmic precursor forms of IL-1β and IL-18.

fact: IL-1β lacks a signal peptide; caspase-1 cleaves gasdermin D, and the N-terminal fragment forms plasma membrane pores through which IL-1β leaves the cell.
quote: caspase-1 cleavage of a cytosolic protein called gasdermin D, removing the inhibitory C-terminal domain and generating an N-terminal fragment that polymerizes to form pores

fact: IL-1β production needs two signals: signal 1 (TLR, NLR or RLR signalling through NF-κB) makes pro-IL-1β; signal 2 activates the inflammasome to cleave it.
quote: IL-1 production usually requires two distinct signals: one that activates new gene transcription and production of a 33-kD precursor pro–IL-1β polypeptide

fact: NLRP3 senses uric acid crystals, alum, cholesterol crystals, extracellular ATP, silica, streptococcal and staphylococcal toxins, and influenza virus.
quote: uric acid crystals, aluminum hydroxide crystals used in vaccine adjuvants, cholesterol crystals, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) released from mitochondria, silica

fact: Common upstream triggers of NLRP3 are reduced cytosolic K+ (K+ efflux) and reactive oxygen species; crystals may act by damaging lysosomal membranes.
quote: Reduced cytoplasmic potassium ion concentration may be one such common mechanism

fact: The adjuvant effect of aluminium hydroxide (alum) depends on NLRP3 and the inflammasome pathway.
quote: aluminum hydroxide (alum) rely on NALP3 and the inflammasome pathway

fact: Pyroptosis is an inflammatory programmed cell death of macrophages and dendritic cells, but not neutrophils, caused by gasdermin D pores; fluid enters, the cell swells and the plasma membrane fails.
quote: an inflammatory form of programmed cell death of macrophages and DCs (but not of neutrophils and most other cell types) called pyroptosis

fact: In the noncanonical pathway, cytosolic LPS activates caspase-4 or caspase-5 in humans (caspase-11 in rodents), which cleaves gasdermin D and causes pyroptosis.
quote: uses a different caspase (caspase-11 in rodents; caspase-4 or caspase-5 in humans)

fact: Other inflammasome sensors are NLRC4 (cytosolic flagellin, type III secretion system), NLRP1 (anthrax lethal toxin), AIM2 (dsDNA) and pyrin (toxins that modify Rho GTPases).
quote: NLRC4 recognizes cytosolic flagellin and components of the type III secretion system of bacteria. NLRP1 recognizes the anthrax lethal toxin.

fact: Phagocytosed monosodium urate crystals damage lysosomes and activate inflammasomes; IL-1 antagonists are used for severe gout resistant to conventional drugs.
quote: IL-1 antagonists have been used to effectively treat cases of severe gout that are resistant to conventional anti-inflammatory drugs.

fact: Gain-of-function inflammasome mutations cause excess IL-1 with recurrent fever and inflammation of skin, joints and abdomen (inflammasomopathies, a subgroup of autoinflammatory syndromes).
quote: The result is recurrent attacks of fever and localized inflammation, most commonly in the skin, joints, and abdominal cavity.

fact: Autoinflammatory diseases differ from autoimmune diseases, which are caused by self-reactive antibodies and/or T cells.
quote: Autoinflammatory diseases are distinct from autoimmune diseases, which are disorders of adaptive immunity caused by antibodies and/or T cells reactive with self antigens.

fact: Mutations in NLRP3 (cryopyrin) cause cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPS).
quote: Autoinflammatory diseases caused by mutations in NLRP3 (also known as cryopyrin) are called cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPS).

fact: Patients with CAPS can be treated successfully with IL-1 antagonists.
quote: Patients with CAPS can be successfully treated with IL-1 antagonists

fact: CAPS is caused by gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations and presents with fever, neutrophilic rash, bony lesions and central nervous system inflammation.
quote: Fever, neutrophilic rash, bony lesions, central nervous system inflammation

fact: Muckle-Wells syndrome and familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome (FCAS) are dominantly inherited NLRP3 disorders with fever (cold-induced in FCAS), urticarial rash, joint pain and conjunctivitis.
quote: episodes of fever—which is induced by exposure to cold in the case of FCAS—as well as urticarial rash, joint pains, and conjunctivitis

fact: Muckle-Wells syndrome also causes progressive deafness.
quote: Periodic fever, urticarial rash, joint pains, conjunctivitis, progressive deafness

fact: NLRP3 mutations also cause chronic infantile neurologic cutaneous and articular syndrome (CINCA), with neonatal-onset fever, urticarial rash, arthropathy and neurological disease.
quote: Mutations in NLRP3 are also associated with the autoinflammatory disorder chronic infantile neurologic cutaneous and articular syndrome (CINCA)

fact: Muckle-Wells syndrome responds dramatically to anakinra, an IL-1 receptor antagonist.
quote: Muckle–Wells syndrome responds dramatically to the drug anakinra, an antagonist of the receptor for IL-1.

fact: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is caused by mutations in MEFV, which encodes pyrin; it presents with fever, serositis and arthritis.
quote: familial Mediterranean fever, caused by mutation of the MEFV gene, which encodes pyrin.

fact: TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome (TRAPS) is caused by mutations in the gene for TNF receptor I, gives periodic fever, myalgia and rash, and responds to TNF blockade.
quote: (TRAPS) is caused by mutations in quite a different gene, that encoding the TNF-a receptor TNFR-I.

fact: Hyper-IgD syndrome (HIDS) is caused by partial mevalonate kinase deficiency and gives fever from infancy, high serum IgD and lymphadenopathy.
quote: is caused by mutations that result in a partial deficiency of mevalonate kinase

fact: RIG-like receptors (RLRs) are cytosolic sensors of viral RNA that induce type I IFNs; the best known are RIG-I and MDA5.
quote: RIG-like receptors (RLRs) are cytosolic sensors of viral RNA that respond by inducing the production of the antiviral type I IFNs

fact: MDA5 recognizes long dsRNA (1-6 kb).
quote: MDA5 recognizes long dsRNA (1–6 kb)

fact: RIG-I recognizes RNA with a 5′-triphosphate, which host cytosolic mRNA does not have because of its 7-methylguanosine cap.
quote: RIG-I will only recognize RNA with a 5′ triphosphate moiety

fact: SARS-CoV-2 RNA vaccines use pseudouridine instead of uridine to reduce detection by innate RNA sensors.
quote: changing uridines to derivatives called pseudouridines, which reduced detection by innate RNA sensors

fact: Activated RLRs bind MAVS on the outer mitochondrial membrane; MAVS polymerizes and recruits TRAF proteins that activate TBK1 and IKK.
quote: the RLRs are recruited to the outer mitochondrial membrane by the MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral-signaling) protein

fact: TBK1 phosphorylates IRF3 and IRF7, and IKK activates NF-κB; these transcription factors induce type I IFNs.
quote: TBK1 phosphorylates and activates IRF3 and IRF7 and IKK activates NF-κB; these transcription factors induce production of type I IFNs.

fact: RIG-I-deficient mice are susceptible to several ssRNA viruses but not picornaviruses; MDA5-deficient mice are susceptible to picornaviruses.
quote: mice deficient in MDA-5 are susceptible to picornaviruses, indicating that these two sensors of viral RNAs have crucial but distinct roles

fact: Cytosolic DNA sensors detect dsDNA from microbes or damaged host cells (micronuclei, mitochondria) and induce type I IFN and autophagy.
quote: Cytosolic DNA sensors (CDSs) are molecules that detect double-stranded (ds) DNA in the cytosol

fact: Cytosolic dsDNA activates the enzyme cGAS, which makes the second messenger cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP).
quote: cytosolic dsDNA activates the enzyme cGAS (cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate [GMP-AMP] synthase), which generates a signaling molecule called cGAMP

fact: STING is an endoplasmic reticulum adaptor that binds cGAMP, moves to the Golgi and activates TBK1, which activates IRF3/IRF7 and NF-κB to induce type I IFN.
quote: STING is an endoplasmic reticulum–localized transmembrane adaptor protein whose cytosolic tail binds to cGAMP with high affinity

fact: Gain-of-function STING mutations cause a type I IFN-driven systemic inflammatory disease of skin and lung (an interferonopathy).
quote: Gain-of-function mutations in the gene that encodes STING result in systemic inflammatory disease with manifestations in skin and lung

fact: STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI) presents with cutaneous vasculopathy, fever and interstitial lung disease.
quote: Cutaneous vasculopathy, fever, and interstitial lung disease

fact: Aicardi-Goutières syndrome is an interferonopathy caused by loss-of-function mutations in nucleases (e.g., TREX1, SAMHD1), so excess nucleic acid reaches the sensors.
quote: Loss of function mutations in genes encoding DNAases and RNAases, excessive DNA and RNA available to nucleic acid sensors

fact: AIM2 binds cytosolic dsDNA and forms an inflammasome that generates active IL-1β.
quote: AIM2 (absent in melanoma-2) is another cytosolic sensor that binds cytosolic dsDNA and forms an inflammasome

fact: The mannose receptor (CD206) on macrophages mediates phagocytosis of microbes with terminal mannose, fucose or N-acetylglucosamine; host glycans usually end in galactose and sialic acid.
quote: eukaryotic cell surface carbohydrates are most often terminated by galactose and sialic acid

fact: Dectin-1 (CD369) binds fungal β-glucan and is required for immunity to Candida, Aspergillus and Pneumocystis.
quote: Dectin-1 (CD369) binds β-glucan, which is a major cell wall component of many fungal species

fact: Dectin-1 and Dectin-2 signal through an ITAM/SYK/CARD9 pathway to NF-κB and promote Th17 differentiation and antifungal immunity.
quote: ITAM/SYK/CARD9 pathway of NF-κB activation

fact: Scavenger receptors such as SR-A and CD36 on macrophages mediate phagocytosis; CD36 is a co-receptor for TLR2/6.
quote: CD36 functions as a coreceptor in TLR2/6 recognition and response to bacterially derived lipoteichoic acid and diacylated lipopeptides

fact: Formyl peptide receptor 1 (FPR1) on leukocytes recognizes N-formylmethionyl peptides, which bacteria and mitochondria make, and directs cell movement.
quote: synthesis of all bacterial proteins and few mammalian proteins (only those synthesized within mitochondria) is initiated by N-formylmethionine

fact: Pentraxins are the short pentraxins CRP and serum amyloid P (SAP) and the long pentraxin PTX3.
quote: the short pentraxins, C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum amyloid P (SAP), and the long pentraxin PTX3

fact: CRP binds phosphorylcholine and SAP binds phosphatidylethanolamine on bacteria and apoptotic cells.
quote: The ligands recognized by CRP and SAP include phosphorylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, respectively

fact: CRP, SAP and PTX3 all activate the classical complement pathway by binding C1q.
quote: CRP, SAP, and PTX3 all activate the classical pathway of complement by binding C1q.

fact: Plasma CRP can rise up to 1000-fold in infection because IL-6, IL-1 and TNF increase its synthesis in the liver.
quote: Plasma concentrations of CRP are very low in healthy individuals but can increase up to 1000-fold during infections

fact: PTX3 is made by dendritic cells, macrophages and endothelial cells, is stored in neutrophil granules and protects mice against Aspergillus fumigatus and influenza.
quote: PTX3 is also stored in neutrophil granules and released as neutrophils die.

fact: Mannose-binding lectin (MBL) is a collectin that binds terminal mannose and fucose and acts as an opsonin; low MBL levels increase infection risk, mainly with other immune defects.
quote: Low MBL levels result in increased susceptibility to a variety of infections, especially in individuals who have other immune defects.

fact: MBL triggers the lectin pathway of complement through MASP1 and MASP2.
quote: The lectin pathway is triggered by a plasma protein called mannose-binding lectin (MBL)

fact: The collectins SP-A and SP-D in lung alveoli bind microbes and act as opsonins for alveolar macrophages.
quote: They bind to various microorganisms and act as opsonins, facilitating ingestion of the microbes by alveolar macrophages.

fact: Ficolins have a fibrinogen-type (not C-type lectin) recognition domain, bind N-acetylglucosamine and lipoteichoic acid, opsonize bacteria and activate complement like MBL.
quote: instead of a C-type lectin domain, they have a fibrinogen-type carbohydrate recognition domain

fact: TNF, mainly from macrophages, activates endothelium and neutrophils, induces acute-phase proteins and fever, and causes cachexia and apoptosis.
quote: Muscle, fat: catabolism (cachexia)

fact: IL-1 activates endothelium, causes fever, induces acute-phase proteins and promotes Th17 differentiation.
quote: Endothelial cells: activation (inflammation, coagulation) Hypothalamus: fever Liver: synthesis of acute-phase proteins T cells: Th17 differentiation

fact: IL-6 induces acute-phase reactants in the liver and promotes differentiation of IL-17-producing helper T cells.
quote: It induces the synthesis of acute-phase reactants by the liver and promotes the differentiation of IL-17–producing helper T cells.

fact: IL-12 from dendritic cells and macrophages stimulates IFN-γ production by ILC1s, NK cells and T cells and promotes Th1 differentiation.
quote: it stimulates IFN-γ production by ILC1s, NK cells, and T cells; enhances NK cell–and CTL-mediated cytotoxicity; and promotes differentiation of Th1 cells

fact: Patients with IL-12 receptor β1 mutations are highly susceptible to Salmonella and mycobacteria.
quote: patients with mutations in the IL-12 receptor β1 subunit are highly susceptible to infections with intracellular bacteria, notably Salmonella and mycobacteria

fact: IL-18, like IL-1, needs the inflammasome for activation; it enhances NK cell functions.
quote: IL-18 enhances the functions of NK cells, similar to IL-12.

fact: Type I IFNs induce an antiviral state and increase MHC class I expression in all cells, and activate NK cells.
quote: All cells: antiviral state, increased MHC-I expression

fact: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells are the major source of IFN-α; many cell types make IFN-β.
quote: Plasmacytoid DCs are the major sources of IFN-α

fact: TNF and IL-1 stimulate secretion of the chemokines CXCL8 and CCL2, which attract neutrophils and monocytes respectively.
quote: TNF and IL-1 also stimulate various cells to secrete chemokines, such as CXCL8 and CCL2, which bind to receptors on neutrophils and monocytes, respectively.

fact: TNF, IL-1 and IL-6 induce hepatocytes to produce acute-phase proteins, including CRP, SAP and fibrinogen.
quote: TNF, IL-1, and IL-6 induce hepatocytes to produce acute-phase proteins, including CRP, SAP, and fibrinogen

fact: Septic shock is mediated in large part by TNF.
quote: Septic shock, a life-threatening condition resulting from severe infections, is mediated in large part by TNF.

fact: IL-33 is stored in the nuclei of barrier epithelial cells and acts as an alarmin when damaged cells release it.
quote: It is often called an alarmin because it is rapidly released from damaged epithelial cells

fact: Mast cells express TLRs, and TLR ligands can induce mast cell degranulation.
quote: Mast cells express TLRs and TLR ligands can induce mast cell degranulation.

fact: In the allergy chapter, TLR ligands are listed among stimuli that make mast cells produce lipid mediators, cytokines and chemokines without degranulation.
quote: These stimuli include Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands; substances released from injured cells, including ATP; fungal glucans

fact: Some DAMPs act through TLRs: heat shock proteins bind TLR4 and HMGB1 binds TLR2.
quote: heat shock proteins (HSPs), which are chaperones induced in response to various cell stresses and bind to TLR4

fact: Type I IFNs from virus-exposed cells act mainly on uninfected neighbouring cells to prevent spread of the virus.
quote: act mainly on other uninfected cells to prevent the spread of viral infection

fact: The MyD88–IRAK4–IRAK1 pathway lies downstream of most TLRs and of the IL-1 receptor and induces proinflammatory cytokines through NF-κB.
quote: The major signaling pathway downstream of most TLRs and of the IL-1 receptor (IL-1R) includes the MyD88 adaptor and the IRAK-4 and IRAK-1 kinases

fact: Janeway describes FMF as autosomal recessive and proposes that absence of functional pyrin leads to unregulated cytokine activity.
quote: It is proposed that an absence of functional pyrin leads to unregulated cytokine activity and defective apoptosis

fact: STING directly senses the bacterial second messengers cyclic di-GMP and cyclic di-AMP.
quote: The bacterial second messenger molecules cyclic di-GMP (c-di-GMP) and cyclic di-AMP (c-di-AMP) are directly sensed by STING.
